recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is; further edits would either duplicate already-applied wording or apply the one proposed change the work group explicitly rejected.
issue_request: FHIR-17463 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-I change request for the core Narrative page. It asked to distinguish normative requirements from informative guidance by changing selected narrative prose to RFC-style SHALL/MAY/SHOULD wording, while the approved resolution explicitly excluded the final proposed change from "The narrative is an XHTML fragment" to "The narrative SHALL BE an XHTML fragment."
initial_application: The issue was applied by d2f5be10b33b56c87d6a9ea51a46d2c48ac7efa1, "GF#17463 - fix normative language," which includes the Jira-commented svn revision 14245 and changed source/narrative.html in the requested places.
additional_context: FHIR-17463 followed FHIR-16480, a Resolved - No Change / Not Persuasive request about narrative normative/informative distinction. source/fhir.ini shows Narrative is an active type page and normative datatype, so source/narrative.html is in current build scope. Zulip and Confluence searches found no relevant conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/narrative.html already says "It SHALL be safe," "MAY define," "MAY contain," "SHOULD include," uses non-normative "can"/"would" in the example guidance, includes the paragraph split before "Systems MAY," and leaves "The narrative is an XHTML fragment" unchanged.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Not Persuasive narrative normative/informative request that explains why FHIR-17463 was a narrower accepted follow-up.
